summary:
FLAME INTELLIGENCE is an interactive, bilingual research prototype that makes spacecraft fire safety research easier to understand. Our team created a website combining NASA combustion investigations (including SAFFIRE, SAME, BASS, ACME and FLEX), atmospheric data, spacecraft material comparisons and educational visualizations. Users can compare research experiments, explore how altitude affects temperature, pressure, density and oxygen partial pressure, and examine past spacecraft incidents alongside researched material or system alternatives. Examples include Beta cloth for cabin textiles, reviewed PTFE cable assemblies and water electrolysis as a different oxygen-generation approach. The platform explains how temperature, gas, pressure, airflow and camera observations may contribute to fire detection.
JavaScript calculations connect users' selections to charts and diagrams. Flame motion and sensor graphics are illustrative, not live measurements or validated forecasts. The result is an accessible research and learning tool that emphasizes evidence, test conditions and limitations rather than claiming to predict a fire probability or guarantee safety
details:
PURPOSE AND USERS: We built a Turkish/English web prototype to help students and other users explore spacecraft combustion research without needing to interpret technical reports alone. RESEARCH: Search and compare NASA SAFFIRE, SAME/SAME-R, BASS, ACME and FLEX investigations by objectives, samples, and environmental conditions. ATMOSPHERE: JavaScript uses U.S. Standard Atmosphere references to show altitude-dependent temperature, pressure and density; oxygen partial pressure is derived from pressure and selected oxygen fraction. Cabin inputs stay separate from external atmospheric conditions. MATERIALS: Paired rocket diagrams compare documented hazards with researched alternatives - Beta cloth and Kevlar/PBI research for cabin textiles, a specifically tested PTFE cable assembly, and water electrolysis as an alternative oxygen-generation system. These are research proposals, not installed or team-tested solutions. DETECTION: The website explains temperature, O2, CO2, pressure, airflow and camera channels and compares published smoke investigations. It is not a working alarm. TOOLS AND LIMITS: The browser interface uses JavaScript, interactive controls, graphics and simple charts. Visual signals are illustrative; there is no live NASA feed, trained

fire-prediction model or experimentally validated numerical fire-risk score. AI assistance was used during project development, with source-based review
